definitions.explanation: A door that opens by sliding sideways along a groove or rail rather than swinging on hinges. Common in traditional Japanese architecture (shoji, fusuma) and also widely used in modern Japanese homes for closets, entryways, and room partitions.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けた→開ける：00563_akeru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|い}り{口|ぐち}→入り口：02507_iriguchi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{引|ひ}き{戸|ど}になっている。
examples.english: The entrance to this room is a sliding door.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{開閉|かいへい}→開閉：06610_kaihei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}らない→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{狭|せま}い→狭い：00750_semai⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}いている→向く：02304_muku⟧。
examples.english: Since sliding doors don't take up space when they open and close, they suit small rooms.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{引|ひ}く→引く：01978_hiku⟧ (to pull) + ⟦{戸|と}→戸：00676_to⟧ (door). Contrasted with hinged doors, which require swing-out clearance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧: to open a sliding door
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧: to close a sliding door
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧: a room with sliding doors

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {開|ひら}き{戸|ど}: hinged door — opens by swinging on hinges
- ⟦{襖|ふすま}→襖：03908_fusuma⟧: fusuma — paper-and-wood sliding panel for interior partitions
- ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧: shoji — sliding screen of translucent paper on a wooden frame
